=== origami --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Experimental SGI emulation

Usage: origami
       origami <COMMAND>

Commands:
  machines                List machine presets, or show one preset's graphics and processor choices
  version                 Show version and Git identity for each bundled executable
  create                  Create a machine configuration and acquire its verified PROM
  validate                Check a machine configuration
  upgrade                 Upgrade a stopped machine created by an earlier Origami
  show                    Show a machine configuration
  show-command            Print the QEMU command without starting the guest
  run                     Start a guest
  status                  Show whether a machine is running
  console                 Connect to a background guest's serial console
  stop                    Stop a background guest
  reset                   Reset a running guest, as its reset button would
  drive-create            Create and attach a new system disk
  drive-attach            Attach an existing disk, CD or tape image; a disk may be a CHD
  drive-detach            Detach a drive without deleting its image
  graphics-set            Change a stopped machine's graphics, where its topology allows that
  console-set             Choose the serial port a stopped guest's console uses
  nvram                   List or change a stopped machine's PROM environment in its NVRAM
  network-set             Change networking on a stopped guest
  network-forward-add     Forward a host loopback port to a guest port
  network-forward-remove  Remove a port forward
  share                   Share a host folder with the guest over NFS, or remove a share
  install-init            Configure install media and private networking without starting the guest
  install-addon           Add an optional package source to an installation
  install-check           Check install media without installing IRIX; remote media are only probed
  install-serve           Serve installation media until stopped
  install-apply           At Inst>, install the selected profile and its add-ons, then restart
  help                    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -V, --version  Show version and Git identity for each bundled executable
  -h, --help     Print help
--- stderr

Experimental SGI emulation

Usage: origami
       origami <COMMAND>

Commands:

=== origami machines --help
exit 0
--- stdout
List machine presets, or show one preset's graphics and processor choices

Usage: origami machines [OPTIONS] [PRESET]

Arguments:
  [PRESET]  Show this preset in detail

Options:
      --all   Show every preset in detail
  -h, --help  Print help

Example: origami machines octane2-vpro

=== origami create --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Create a machine configuration and acquire its verified PROM

Usage: origami create [OPTIONS] --preset <PRESET> <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  Destination machine directory

Options:
      --preset <PRESET>        Machine preset from origami machines
      --prom <FILE>            Local boot PROM instead of a download
      --io-prom <FILE>         Local IO PROM for presets with a BASEIO or GIGAchannel board
      --processor <ID>         Processor module, for presets that offer a choice (see origami machines)
      --memory-per-node <MiB>  Memory per node in MiB
  -h, --help                   Print help

Graphics options:
      --graphics <PRODUCT>             Graphics product, such as si, v12 or ir2, or none for no graphics; omit for the preset's
      --graphics-slot <SLOT>           Slot for the pipe, such as io3 or widget-11; omit for the preset's or the machine's usual slot
      --graphics-pipes <N>             How many pipes of that product the machine fits, such as 4 for an Onyx 3400; see origami machines PRESET for its limit
      --graphics-setting <NAME=VALUE>  A pipe setting other than its default, such as rm-count=1; repeatable

Hardware options:
      --mac <MAC>                The machine's Ethernet address, for its identity and onboard network
      --emu-id <N>               The machine's emu-id, 1 to 2999, which its host id and, unless --mac is given, its Ethernet address derive from. Without it `create` takes the lowest free number; 3000 and up are reserved for harness and CI machines
      --set <NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE>  Give a machine input its preset takes, such as board-id-word=0x4000, prid=0xe24 or, for a list, chassis-eeprom.0=FILE; repeatable. origami machines PRESET lists them

Example: origami create o200 --preset origin200-1
--- stderr

exit 0
--- stdout
Upgrade a stopped machine created by an earlier Origami

Usage: origami upgrade [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  

Options:
      --prom <FILE>     Local boot PROM instead of a download, for a machine that needs one
      --io-prom <FILE>  Local IO PROM for a machine with a BASEIO or GIGAchannel board
  -h, --help            Print help

=== origami show-command --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Print the QEMU command without starting the guest

Usage: origami show-command [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>
          Machine directory

Options:
      --display <DISPLAY>
          Local window, VNC server, shared-memory display or no graphics

          Possible values:
          - local
          - vnc
          - shm:   Publish the display through shared memory for origami-gui
          - none

      --vnc-port <VNC_PORT>
          VNC TCP port (default 5900)

      --display-gpu <UUID>
          With --display shm: the Vulkan deviceUUID (32 hex digits) of the viewer's adapter, so QEMU exports scanout memory the viewer imports without a copy

      --qemu-arg <ARG>
          Extra QEMU argument, appended after the `[qemu] extra-args` of machine.toml (repeatable; unsupported and not validated)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
--- stderr
=== origami run --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Start a guest

Usage: origami run [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>
          Machine directory

Options:
      --display <DISPLAY>
          Local window, VNC server, shared-memory display or no graphics

          Possible values:
          - local
          - vnc
          - shm:   Publish the display through shared memory for origami-gui
          - none

      --vnc-port <VNC_PORT>
          VNC TCP port (default 5900)

      --display-gpu <UUID>
          With --display shm: the Vulkan deviceUUID (32 hex digits) of the viewer's adapter, so QEMU exports scanout memory the viewer imports without a copy

      --qemu-arg <ARG>
          Extra QEMU argument, appended after the `[qemu] extra-args` of machine.toml (repeatable; unsupported and not validated)

      --background
          Run with console and installer control connections

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  origami run o200
  origami run o200 --display vnc --vnc-port 5900

=== origami stop --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Stop a background guest

Usage: origami stop [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  Machine directory

Options:
      --force  Kill QEMU instead of asking it to quit. The guest does not sync its disks and a CHD disk's changes stay in its .diff.chd file
  -h, --help   Print help
--- stderr

=== origami drive-attach --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Attach an existing disk, CD or tape image; a disk may be a CHD

Usage: origami drive-attach [OPTIONS] --type <KIND> --target <TARGET> <DIR> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <DIR>   
  <FILE>  

Options:
      --type <KIND>      [possible values: disk, cdrom, tape]
      --target <TARGET>  
      --overlay          Keep a CHD disk's writes in its .diff.chd file instead of folding them into the image when the machine stops
  -h, --help             Print help

exit 0
--- stdout
Change a stopped machine's graphics, where its topology allows that

Usage: origami graphics-set [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Graphics options:
      --graphics <PRODUCT>             Graphics product, such as si, v12 or ir2, or none for no graphics; omit for the preset's
      --graphics-slot <SLOT>           Slot for the pipe, such as io3 or widget-11; omit for the preset's or the machine's usual slot
      --graphics-pipes <N>             How many pipes of that product the machine fits, such as 4 for an Onyx 3400; see origami machines PRESET for its limit
      --graphics-setting <NAME=VALUE>  A pipe setting other than its default, such as rm-count=1; repeatable

No graphics can change after a machine is created yet; create a new machine instead.

exit 0

Choose the serial port a stopped guest's console uses

Usage: origami console-set [OPTIONS] <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  

Options:
      --port <PORT>  Serial line to connect, named as in QEMU's machine list (such as l1 or ioc3_a); omit to use the machine's default console
  -h, --help         Print help
--- stderr
=== origami nvram --help
exit 0
--- stdout
List or change a stopped machine's PROM environment in its NVRAM

Usage: origami nvram <DIR> [COMMAND]

Commands:
  get   Show one variable
  set   Set variables and recompute the checksum
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  <DIR>  Machine directory

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Examples:
  origami nvram octane
  origami nvram octane get console
  origami nvram octane set console=d AutoLoad=Yes
--- stderr
=== origami network-set --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Change networking on a stopped guest

Usage: origami network-set [OPTIONS] --mode <MODE> <DIR>

Arguments:
  <DIR>  

Options:
      --mode <MODE>                     [possible values: user, none, private, tap, vmnet]
      --endpoint <ENDPOINT>             Instigator's private network endpoint, or the socket_vmnet socket; a private network without one is hosted by `run`
      --interface <INTERFACE>           Tap device on Linux, or TAP-Windows6 adapter name on Windows
      --share-address <ADDRESS/PREFIX>  Where shares are served on a tap or vmnet network, such as 192.168.1.50/24: a free address on that network
      --subnet <A.B.C.0/24>             The private /24 that user and private networking use, such as 10.42.0.0/24 (default 10.98.0.0/24); it stays set across mode changes
      --mac <MAC>                       Machine MAC, when it has none yet
  -h, --help                            Print help
--- stderr

exit 0

Forward a host loopback port to a guest port

Usage: origami network-forward-add --protocol <PROTOCOL> --host-port <HOST_PORT> --guest-port <GUEST_PORT> <DIR> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <DIR>   
  <NAME>  

Options:
      --protocol <PROTOCOL>      [possible values: tcp, udp]
      --host-port <HOST_PORT>    
      --guest-port <GUEST_PORT>  
  -h, --help                     Print help

=== origami share --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Share a host folder with the guest over NFS, or remove a share

Usage: origami share [OPTIONS] <DIR> <NAME> [HOSTDIR]

Arguments:
  <DIR>      
  <NAME>     The name the guest mounts, as ADDRESS:/NAME
  [HOSTDIR]  The host folder to share

Options:
      --remove  Remove the share
  -h, --help    Print help

Examples:
  origami share o200 src ~/code
  origami share o200 src --remove
--- stderr

  <DIR>  

Options:
      --media-root <DIR>   
      --mac <MAC>          Machine MAC, when it has none yet
      --profile <PROFILE>  [default: standard] [possible values: minimal, standard]
      --release <RELEASE>  IRIX release to install [default: 6.5.30] [possible values: 6.5.22, 6.5.30]
  -h, --help               Print help

  <DIR>

      --name <NAME>           Add-on name; mipspro and rad4 need no --source
      --source <PATH-OR-URL>  
      --install <INSTALL>     
      --base <BASE>           
      --dist <DIST>           
      --media-root <DIR>      Local media for a named add-on, the directory containing mipspro/
  -h, --help                  Print help

=== origami machines --all
exit 0
--- stdout
origin200-1: Origin 200, 1 CPU, 256 MiB per node, no graphics

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  rad4     RAD4
  rad4-km  RAD4-KM
  none (default)

Slots: pci-5, pci-6, pci-7

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):
  prid (integer), default 0x926 (inferred)
  dip-switches (integer) names no-diag heavy-diag mfg-diag verbose global-pod
    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags
  junk-uart (boolean)

Processor modules (create --processor ID): r10000-180mhz-1mb (default),
  r10000-180mhz-2mb, r10000-225mhz-2mb, r12000-270mhz-4mb

    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags
  junk-uart (boolean)

Processor modules (create --processor ID): r10000-180mhz-1mb (default),
  r10000-180mhz-2mb, r10000-225mhz-2mb, r12000-270mhz-4mb

origin200-impact: Origin 200, 1 CPU, 256 MiB per node, SI (GIGAchannel) in io6

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  si       Solid IMPACT (SI) (default)
  si-t     SI with texture
  ssi      SSI
  mxi      MXI
  esi      ESI
  esi-t    ESI with texture
  essi     ESSI
  emxi     EMXI
  rad4     RAD4
  rad4-km  RAD4-KM
  none

Slots: io6, pci-5, pci-6, pci-7

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality: SGI did not offer InfiniteReality on the Origin 200, and the
    known GIGAchannel pipe is an owner conversion the model does not build

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):
  prid (integer), default 0x926 (inferred)
  dip-switches (integer) names no-diag heavy-diag mfg-diag verbose global-pod
    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags
  junk-uart (boolean)

Processor modules (create --processor ID): r10000-180mhz-1mb (default),
  r10000-180mhz-2mb, r10000-225mhz-2mb, r12000-270mhz-4mb

origin2000-impact: Origin 2000 deskside, 2 CPUs, 256 MiB per node, SI in io3

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  si     Solid IMPACT (SI) (default)
  si-t   SI with texture
  ssi    SSI
  mxi    MXI
  esi    ESI
  esi-t  ESI with texture
  essi   ESSI
  emxi   EMXI
  none

Slots: io2, io3, io4, io5, io6

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality: an Origin 2000 with an InfiniteReality pipe is an Onyx2, so
    use onyx2-deskside

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):
  prid (integer), default 0x926 (inferred)
  dip-switches (integer) names no-diag heavy-diag mfg-diag verbose global-pod
    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags

origin2000-8: Origin 2000 rack, 8 CPUs, 256 MiB per node, no graphics

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  si     Solid IMPACT (SI)
  si-t   SI with texture
  ssi    SSI
  mxi    MXI
  esi    ESI
  esi-t  ESI with texture
  essi   ESSI
  emxi   EMXI
  none (default)

Slots: io2, io3, io4, io5, io6, io7, io8, io9, io10, io11, io12

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality: an Origin 2000 with an InfiniteReality pipe is an Onyx2, so
    use onyx2-rack

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):
  prid (integer), default 0x926 (inferred)
  dip-switches (integer) names no-diag heavy-diag mfg-diag verbose global-pod
    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags

onyx2-infinite-reality: Onyx2 deskside, 4 CPUs, 256 MiB per node,
    InfiniteReality2 in io4

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  ir2   InfiniteReality2 (default)
        settings: geometry=ge14-4*|ge14-2, rm-count=1|2*,
                  display=dg5-8*|dg5-2|dg5-2-gvo
  ir2e  InfiniteReality2E
        settings: rm-count=1|2*, display=dg5-8*|dg5-2|dg5-2-gvo

Slots: io4

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality with rm-count=4: a pipe with no Ktown is an Onyx2 deskside
    pipe, which holds at most two raster managers
  InfiniteReality3: no manual or capture places an InfiniteReality3 in an Onyx2
    deskside
  No graphics: SGI sold no Onyx2 without an InfiniteReality pipe, and an Onyx2
    with no pipe is an Origin 2000, so use origin2000-deskside or
    origin2000-rack

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):
  prid (integer), default 0x926 (inferred)
  dip-switches (integer) names no-diag heavy-diag mfg-diag verbose global-pod
    local-pod no-mem-pod default-env bypass-io6 no-global-master pod
    skip-prom-diags

onyx2-rack-infinite-reality: Onyx2 rack, 1 CPU, 256 MiB per node,
    InfiniteReality3 in io3

Graphics (create --graphics PRODUCT [--graphics-slot SLOT]; * = default):
  ir2e  InfiniteReality2E
        settings: rm-count=1*|2|4, display=dg5-2*|dg5-8|dg5-2-gvo
  ir3   InfiniteReality3 (default)
        settings: rm-count=1*|2|4, display=dg5-2*|dg5-8|dg5-2-gvo

Pipes: 1 to 2 (create --graphics-pipes N); a pipe on a node board the preset
  lacks adds that node

Slots: io3

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality2: no manual or capture places a GE14 InfiniteReality2 in an
    Onyx2 rack
  No graphics: SGI sold no Onyx2 without an InfiniteReality pipe, and an Onyx2
    with no pipe is an Origin 2000, so use origin2000-deskside or
    origin2000-rack

Settings (create --set NAME[.SLOT]=VALUE):

        settings: rm-count=1*|2|4, display=dg5-2*|dg5-8|dg5-2-gvo

Pipes: 1 to 4 (create --graphics-pipes N); a pipe on a node board the preset
  lacks adds that node

Slots: gbrick0-pipe0-pipe, gbrick0-pipe1-pipe, gbrick1-pipe0-pipe,
  gbrick1-pipe1-pipe

Not offered:
  InfiniteReality2: the G-brick pipe layer is an InfiniteReality3 pipe, and no
    other revision is modelled for the G-brick
  InfiniteReality2E: the G-brick pipe layer is an InfiniteReality3 pipe, and no
    other revision is modelled for the G-brick
  InfiniteReality3 with rm-count=4: a G-brick's pipe 1 takes one or two raster
    managers; only pipe 0 takes four
  No graphics: an Onyx 3400 with InfiniteReality is sold with G-bricks; a system
    with none is an Origin 3400, so use origin3400
